title: तिहारलाई लक्षित गर्दै साढे ६४ करोडको झिलिमिली बत्ती आयात
content:
काठमाडौं । तिहारलाई लक्षित गर्दै चालु आर्थिक वर्ष २०८३/८४ को पहिलो तीन महिनामा ६४ करोड ५२ लाख रुपैयाँ बराबरको झिलिमिली बत्ती आयात भएको छ । भन्सार विभागको तथ्यांकअनुसार असोजसम्म २८ लाख ५९ हजार थान झिलिमिली बत्ती आयात भएका हुन् । गत आर्थिक वर्षको सोही अवधिमा ५९ करोड ६५ लाख रुपैयाँ बराबरका ३८ लाख ९२ हजार थान बत्ती आयात भएका थिए । यस वर्ष आयातको मूल्य करिब ८ प्रतिशत बढे पनि परिमाण भने करिब २७ प्रतिशत घटेको छ । नेपाल विद्युतीय व्यवसायी महासंघका पूर्वअध्यक्ष सुदर्शनप्रसाद पौडेलका अनुसार कच्चा पदार्थको मूल्य, अमेरिकी डलरको विनिमय दर र ढुवानी खर्च बढ्दा विद्युतीय सामग्रीको मूल्य १५ देखि २० प्रतिशतसम्म वृद्धि भएको छ । उनका अनुसार विद्युतीय सामग्री उत्पादन तथा आयातमा प्रयोग हुने अधिकांश कच्चा पदार्थ चीनबाट र केही भारतबाट आउने गरेका छन् । विशेषगरी चीनबाट आउने सामग्रीको मूल्य स्रोत बजारमै बढेकाले नेपाली बजारमा त्यसको असर परेको उनले बताए । झिलिमिली बत्तीमा प्रयोग हुने तामाको तारदेखि बाहिरी आवरणमा प्रयोग हुने प्लास्टिकसम्मका कच्चा पदार्थको मूल्य बढेको पौडेलले जानकारी दिए । उनले भने, ‘झिलिमिली बत्तीभित्र प्रयोग हुने तार, तामाको मूल्य र तारको आवरणका रूपमा प्रयोग हुने प्लास्टिकको मूल्य पनि बढेको छ । सामग्री उत्पादनमा प्रयोग हुने अधिकांश कच्चा पदार्थको मूल्य स्रोत बजारमै बढेको अवस्था छ ।’ कच्चा पदार्थको मूल्यसँगै अमेरिकी डलरको विनिमय दर बढ्दा पनि आयात लागत वृद्धि भएको उनको भनाइ छ । ‘डलर अघिल्लो वर्षभन्दा यस वर्ष बढेको र कच्चा पदार्थको लागत पनि वृद्धि भएकाले स्रोत बजारमै पर्ने प्रतियुनिट मूल्य बढेको हो,’ उनले भने । ढुवानी खर्चमा भएको वृद्धिले पनि आयातित सामग्री महँगिएको छ । पौडेलका अनुसार अघिल्लो वर्ष एउटा कन्टेनरको ढुवानी खर्च २ हजारदेखि २ हजार २०० अमेरिकी डलर थियो । अहिले ६ हजार डलर तिर्दासमेत कन्टेनर सहजै पाउन नसकिने अवस्था छ । ढुवानी खर्च करिब तीन गुणासम्म बढ्दा त्यसको भार अन्ततः उपभोक्ताले खरिद गर्ने सामग्रीको मूल्यमा पर्ने उनले बताए । चीनसँग जोडिएको केरुङ नाकाबाट नियमित रूपमा सामग्री ल्याउन नसक्दा पनि आयात लागत बढेको पौडेलले बताए । केरुङ नाकाबाट सामान ल्याउँदा तुलनात्मक रूपमा कम खर्च पर्ने भए पनि अहिले वीरगन्जलगायत अन्य भन्सार नाकाबाट घुमाएर ल्याउनुपर्ने अवस्था रहेको उनले जानकारी दिए । पौडेलका अनुसार बजारमा विद्युतीय सामग्रीको माग रहे पनि आपूर्ति पक्ष कमजोर बनेको छ । अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा यस वर्ष धेरै व्यवसायीसँग पर्याप्त मौज्दात छैन । मूल्य बढे पनि कारोबारको परिमाण भने सोही अनुपातमा बढ्न नसकेको उनले बताए । कच्चा पदार्थ, डलरको विनिमय दर र ढुवानी खर्च बढ्नुका साथै आपूर्तिमा समेत समस्या देखिएकाले यस वर्ष तिहारमा झिलिमिली बत्तीको मूल्य गत वर्षभन्दा महँगो पर्ने व्यवसायीको भनाइ छ । पार्वती भण्डारी,नेपाल न्यूज बैंक Kathmandu. In the first three months of the current fiscal year 2083/84, targeting Tihar, 645.2 million rupees worth of twinkle lights have been imported. According to the data of the Customs Department, 2.859 million twinkle lights have been imported till Asoj. During the same period of the last fiscal year, 3.892 million lamps worth Rs 596.5 million were imported. This year, although the value of imports has increased by about 8 percent, the volume has decreased by about 27 percent. According to Sudarshan Prasad Poudel, former president of the Federation of Nepal Electrical Contractors, the price of electrical goods has increased by 15 to 20 percent due to the increase in the price of raw materials, the exchange rate of the US dollar, and transportation costs. According to him, most of the raw materials used in the production and import of electronic equipment come from China and some from India. He said that the price of materials especially from China has increased in the source market, which has affected the Nepali market. Poudel informed that the prices of raw materials, from copper wire used in twinkling lights to plastic used in the outer casing, have increased. He said, "The price of wire used inside twinkling lights, copper, and the price of plastic used as the casing of the wire have also increased. The prices of most of the raw materials used in the production of materials have increased in the source market." He said that the increase in the exchange rate of the US dollar along with the price of raw materials has also increased the cost of imports. "The dollar has increased this year compared to the previous year and the cost of raw materials has also increased, so the per-unit price in the source market has increased," he said. The increase in transportation costs has also made imported materials more expensive. According to Poudel, the transportation cost of a container last year was 2,000 to 2,200 US dollars. Now, even paying 6,000 dollars makes it difficult to get a container. He said that when transportation costs increase by about three times, the burden will ultimately be passed on to the consumers. Poudel said that the cost of imports has increased due to the inability to regularly bring materials through the Kerung border crossing with China. Although it costs relatively less to bring goods through the Kerung border crossing, he informed that now there is a situation where goods have to be brought through other customs checkpoints including Birgunj. According to Poudel, although there is demand for electrical goods in the market, the supply side has become weak. This year, many entrepreneurs do not have sufficient stock compared to the previous year. He said that even though prices have increased, the volume of transactions has not increased in the same proportion. Entrepreneurs say that the price of jingle lights will be more expensive this year during Tihar than last year due to the increase in raw materials, the dollar exchange rate and transportation costs, as well as problems in supply. Parvati Bhandari, Nepal News Bank

पौडेलका अनुसार बजारमा विद्युतीय सामग्रीको माग रहे पनि आपूर्ति पक्ष कमजोर बनेको छ । अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा यस वर्ष धेरै व्यवसायीसँग पर्याप्त मौज्दात छैन । मूल्य बढे पनि कारोबारको परिमाण भने सोही अनुपातमा बढ्न नसकेको उनले बताए । कच्चा पदार्थ, डलरको विनिमय दर र ढुवानी खर्च बढ्नुका साथै आपूर्तिमा समेत समस्या देखिएकाले यस वर्ष तिहारमा झिलिमिली बत्तीको मूल्य गत वर्षभन्दा महँगो पर्ने व्यवसायीको भनाइ छ ।

पार्वती भण्डारी,नेपाल न्यूज बैंक

Kathmandu. In the first three months of the current fiscal year 2083/84, targeting Tihar, 645.2 million rupees worth of twinkle lights have been imported. According to the data of the Customs Department, 2.859 million twinkle lights have been imported till Asoj. During the same period of the last fiscal year, 3.892 million lamps worth Rs 596.5 million were imported. This year, although the value of imports has increased by about 8 percent, the volume has decreased by about 27 percent. According to Sudarshan Prasad Poudel, former president of the Federation of Nepal Electrical Contractors, the price of electrical goods has increased by 15 to 20 percent due to the increase in the price of raw materials, the exchange rate of the US dollar, and transportation costs. According to him, most of the raw materials used in the production and import of electronic equipment come from China and some from India. He said that the price of materials especially from China has increased in the source market, which has affected the Nepali market. Poudel informed that the prices of raw materials, from copper wire used in twinkling lights to plastic used in the outer casing, have increased. He said, "The price of wire used inside twinkling lights, copper, and the price of plastic used as the casing of the wire have also increased. The prices of most of the raw materials used in the production of materials have increased in the source market." He said that the increase in the exchange rate of the US dollar along with the price of raw materials has also increased the cost of imports. "The dollar has increased this year compared to the previous year and the cost of raw materials has also increased, so the per-unit price in the source market has increased," he said. The increase in transportation costs has also made imported materials more expensive. According to Poudel, the transportation cost of a container last year was 2,000 to 2,200 US dollars. Now, even paying 6,000 dollars makes it difficult to get a container. He said that when transportation costs increase by about three times, the burden will ultimately be passed on to the consumers. Poudel said that the cost of imports has increased due to the inability to regularly bring materials through the Kerung border crossing with China. Although it costs relatively less to bring goods through the Kerung border crossing, he informed that now there is a situation where goods have to be brought through other customs checkpoints including Birgunj. According to Poudel, although there is demand for electrical goods in the market, the supply side has become weak. This year, many entrepreneurs do not have sufficient stock compared to the previous year. He said that even though prices have increased, the volume of transactions has not increased in the same proportion. Entrepreneurs say that the price of jingle lights will be more expensive this year during Tihar than last year due to the increase in raw materials, the dollar exchange rate and transportation costs, as well as problems in supply. Parvati Bhandari, Nepal News Bank
